body: Listening to relaxing music, such as classical or jazz, can relieve some of the boredom of studying.
Creating a compare/contrast chart is helpful when studying complex theories and models, or for studying multiple theories in a single chapter.
Splitting the material into chunks can be beneficial. That way, you keep track of what you’ve accomplished, instead of looking at the big picture and getting overwhelmed.
Motivation is an important factor that will help you to study well. This is not a complicated art or unusual technique. It is as simple as remembering to feed yourself daily.
Reward yourself for studying. This will keep you going.
If you study a little bit everyday you’ll be continually reviewing things in your mind. This helps you to understand information, and helps to avoid the stress of last minute cramming.
You could try reading your notes aloud and discussing them with other people. You might want to even record an audio of key points and play it back for yourself.
Set reminder alarms. Having regular reminders keeps you accountable and on track.
Sometimes you can’t force yourself to have the right mindset, and during these times you should simply avoid studying.
Focus on the exam. Knowing the material is only part of it. Do as many mock exams as possible to practice timing and question types.
Set time limits! Before you start your study session, have a look at your to do list and give yourself a set time for each task.
Try to be positive! When studying, remind yourself of your skills and abilities.
If you prepare your own study materials then you’ll learn what you have studied twice: once when you make the study materials, and again when you use them to study.
If you are a visual learner, it can help to create diagrams to visualize how the concepts you are learning relate to one another.
Decide what to study beforehand. This means mapping out what you’ll study, when and for how long. Once you’ve set a schedule, stick to it!
Whether you are a freshman or a senior, these study hacks can make your life easier, and will improve your grades.
Only listen to music that improves your focus.
Quiz yourself! Once you feel like you understand a concept or a topic, it’s important to test yourself.
A straight back chair, that isn’t too comfortable, is the best to study in. You don’t want to get too cozy!
Get creative with online study tools. Try using study tools to help you study better and find what works best for you.
Avoid daydreaming by asking yourself questions about the material as you study.
Memory games, or mnemonic devices, are methods for remembering pieces of information using a simple association of common words.

The old age adage, practice makes perfect, is true. You can practice by yourself by testing yourself with either practice exams, past quizzes, or flash cards (depending what kind of course it is and what’s available).
Make sure you are studying in a clean, quiet and orderly room. Keep anything and everything away from where you are that may cause you to get distracted.
Turn on the light. Studying in a dark room is not recommended.

Consider turning the TV off. This tip varies depending on the individual. Some prefer studying in a tranquil environment devoid of any noise, whereas others prefer studying while listening to music, leaving the TV on at a low volume, etc.
Decide if music is right for you. Music's effect on memory performance varies between individuals.
Get plenty of rest the night before.

Eat a healthy, light meal. Eat a balanced breakfast full of lean protein, vegetables, omega-3 fatty acids, and antioxidants. A sample breakfast might include a spinach omelet with smoked salmon, whole wheat toast, and a banana.
It is a good idea to eat a mint or two before the exam, because some scientists say that it boost memory for a little while.
Get to the exam room with time to spare. Give yourself at least five or 10 minutes to gather your thoughts before starting the exam.
Anyone can concentrate on study if one gets interested in it.When you will study subjects with interest and enthusiasm you will get best out of it.
Don't study when you're really tired. It's better to get a good night's sleep after studying for a short time, than to push on at two in the morning.
Always study when you have the chance. Don't let your mind tell you that you don't want to study.

Study for your learning style. If you're a visual learner, using pictures can help. Auditory learners should record themselves saying notes and recite it afterwards. If you are a physical person lecture to yourself (out loud) while also using your hands or moving around; this way it will be easier for you to memorize.

Different subjects call for different studying. If it's math you're studying for, work on the problems. Don't just read over it like you would for a history class, because you can actually do math, but you can seldom do history.
Think of your teacher. Ask yourself: What is my teacher most likely to ask on the exam? What materials should I focus on to give myself the best chance of knowing what I need to know? And etc.

If you need help, ask someone who is good at these subjects. Friends, family, teachers are all good options. If you don't understand what the person helping you is communicating, don't be afraid to ask them to elaborate.
Make sure you actually pay attention in class. You wouldn't want to miss something that will be tested.
Before you start studying you have to get a good focus on the objectives of your work.
Anything you read... Don't just read it. Understand it fully then you'll not need to read it again.
Do some research on the exam. Finding out who is writing the exam can be helpful. This way, you might be able to understand what sort of questions will be used.
Budget your time wisely to ensure that you cover all the topics covered in the exam.
Write yourself a study guide. Go through your notes and rewrite the most important information.
Take breaks. You need some time to have fun and it is better to revise when you are feeling relaxed than to exhaust yourself studying all day!
Think positive but work hard. Never think you won't be able to pass the exam. Always think positive. If you say you can: you can. If you say you can't: you can't.

Working with other people can help you cover gaps in your own knowledge and also help you remember more information, since you may have to explain things to them or have conversations about the topic.
Do not study a subject only once. If you have more time you can revise for your studies twice or thrice, but only if you have a lot of time and have revised for all your other subjects at least once.
Don't include too many snacks in your daily study routine because you might end up gaining weight instead of knowledge!
When you are done studying,take time to evaluate how successful you have been.
